newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends stronger, pulls others higher.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends stronger, pulls others higher.

text.p: Base metals prices ended firmer across the board on Monday afternoon, led by an eleventh-hour spurt in copper.
Trading on the London Metal Exchange (LME) was dulled by New York's absence due to the U.S. President's Day holiday. Third Wednesday pricing passed routinely.
But copper popped up from lows around $2,250 per tonne in the morning, and then managed to pushed higher on short covering towards the end of the afternoon kerb.
Three months copper ended the kerb at $2,278, up $21 from Friday's kerb close.
"The market has seen copper hold at support over the past few trading days, and it's probably taking some strength from that," said analyst Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff.
"Technically it still looks good and the market is still looking at $2,300 and then the $2,313 resistance level," he added.
The market was expecting a small movement of 3,000-5,000 tonnes in LME stocks, but traders were mixed as to which way they would go.
The market would watch carefully in the near future to see whether stocks would continue rising despite an easier backwardation.
Cash to threes backwardation was last at $55/$60, about $10 down from morning levels and $30 from Friday.
Dealers said they were still wary of the spread narrowing further as so far there were few signs that recent tightness was being rolled forward.
Aluminium crept higher with copper, ending at near its day's highs at $1,570 versus $1,564 on Friday.
But resistance at that level and then at $1,580 was likely to prove difficult for aluminium ,traders said.
Tin, buoyed by consumer buying, was up $50 at $6,025.
Zinc was up by $5.00 at $1,215, boosted by an expected stocks fall on Tuesday.
Nickel traded in a very tight range and ended just $10 higher at $7,750.
Lead, the only metal to end on the minus side of the column, was down just $1.00 at $655.
Alloy was last indicated at $1,480/85, from $1,470/75.
